八重善.name: Yaezen
八重善.desc: A shop standing in the fiercely competitive stretch of the Okinawa Soba Highway (Prefectural Route 84). It offers good-value set menus that pair a gentle soup rich with bonito broth with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) and two small side dishes. Also known for its squid ink soba.
t: Prefectural Route 84, known as the "Okinawa Soba Highway," is a fiercely competitive area with lots of Okinawa soba shops, and in May 2023 I went to eat at one of them, "Yaezen" 😄
Yaezen

I went in at lunchtime on a weekday, but there weren't that many customers and I got in right away 😄　The staff bring the menu to your table and take it back right after you order, so it isn't left on the table, and I forgot to take a photo of it ^^;　Sorry m(_ _)m
The "recommended menu" items are all set meals, and this time I ordered the "Soki Soba Set (small)."
"Soki Soba Set (small)" ¥880

Along with a small soki soba, it came with jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) (seasoned mixed rice), which in Okinawa is a standard at home for celebrations and as an offering at the family Buddhist altar, a small dish of nigana? (it looked something like that; I don't think it was nigana) dressed with canned tuna, a small dish of boiled spinach with dried baby sardines, pickled red ginger for the soba, and, though it's not in the photo, yellow fukujinzuke pickles behind the soba. A pretty decent amount of food 😆

The soki soba has a gentle flavor while the bonito broth comes through, and it's delicious 😋　The noodles were a medium-thin straight type and slightly on the soft side. The pork spare ribs (soki) had an ordinary seasoning, were tender, and had soaked up the flavor nicely; they were delicious.

Rating (9.5/15): The bonito broth soup is nice ✌. Overall it was solidly tasty too. There are still so many more Okinawa soba shops along the "Okinawa Soba Highway" on Route 84, and it really hit me that I've still got a long way to go before conquering them all ^^;　I'll keep making the rounds steadily while enjoying myself 😄

八重食堂.name: Yae Shokudo
八重食堂.desc: A long-established shop in downtown Nago, founded in 1973. Its famous signature is the unique style where you pour the soup yourself from a kettle into a bowl holding only noodles and toppings. A gentle, clear bonito broth with the flat noodles typical of Nago and tender pork spare ribs (soki). Reasonably priced, with soki soba at ¥500.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," so I ate here in July 2020 😄
Yae Soba (it's in downtown Nago, a fiercely competitive area for soba shops lol. It has character, doesn't it)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Yae Shokudo" is featured as shop 3 of 41
I ordered the "Soki Soba," which was introduced with a photo in the map
Soki soba　¥500　Cheap ^^;

The special feature here is that a bowl with just the noodles (no soup) and the toppings is placed on the table, and the soup is brought in a kettle ^^;　This system is unique to Yae Shokudo 😁　The soup is a clear bonito broth with a gentle flavor. The noodles are the flat type. The pork spare ribs (soki) are tender and delicious too. Since the soup alone comes in a kettle, you can drink plenty of broth 😄
Rating (9/15): Yae Shokudo, with its style of bringing the soup in a kettle, is famous. Please give it a try at least once.
PS: There's no parking lot, so you'll have to use a nearby coin parking lot (¥200).

前田食堂（名護店）.name: Maeda Shokudo (Nago branch)
前田食堂（名護店）.desc: The second Nago branch of the famous "Maeda Shokudo" in Ogimi Village. Its signature "Beef Soba" has overwhelming volume with a towering mountain of bean sprouts, and a punchy, peppery soup. Take it on when you're hungry.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in December 2020 😄
Maeda Shokudo, Nago branch
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Maeda Shokudo, Nago branch" is featured as shop 38 of 41
Menu
When you say "Maeda Shokudo," the original is in Ogimi Village, but this shop is the second branch. I ordered the "Beef Soba," which is famous at the main shop too 😄
Beef soba　¥800　There it is! The impact is way too much lol

I went to the main shop in Ogimi Village quite a long time ago, and the second branch is the same: the portions are as generous as ever ^^;　A huge heap of bean sprouts, and the soup is peppery and has a punch 😄　You can't reach the noodles unless you eat the beef and bean sprouts first ^^;　If you're a light eater, the small size is better.
Rating (9/15): I think every menu item at Maeda Shokudo comes in a big portion, so when you visit, please come on an empty stomach ☺

千代.name: Chiyo
千代.desc: A shop in Kin Town, the spring training camp site of the Rakuten Eagles (Mendokoro Chiyo). Inside are tatami-mat seating areas, with rows of autographs from pro baseball players and celebrities such as HY. Its signature is Chiyo Soba, with a slightly rich pork bone-based soup and chewy medium-thin straight noodles. It also has a sister shop in Osaka.
t: This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) and partly added to by me lol 🍜✨
I ate here in October 2024 😊　This time I'm introducing "Chiyo Soba" in Kin Town 😊
Chiyo

This shop operates in Kin Town, known as the spring training camp site of the Tohoku Rakuten Golden Eagles. Lots of autograph boards from baseball players are displayed inside, giving it an atmosphere baseball fans will love 😆
Pro baseball players' autographs displayed inside the shop
Celebrities' autographs displayed inside the shop (there's HY's autograph 😄)
Inside the shop
Menu
Inside, tatami-mat seating areas spread out, and it has a calm atmosphere. Looking at the menu, "Chiyo Soba" is listed at the top as the signature item, so this time I decided to order it.
Chiyo Soba (large)　¥950
First, a sip of the soup. The pork bone-based soup has a firm saltiness and is seasoned on the rich side. This might be a matter of personal preference 🤔
Chiyo Soba (large)　¥950

Next, the noodles. They're a medium-thin straight type, and although the shop doesn't advertise it, they might be homemade fresh noodles. They have a chewy texture and moderate firmness, and my impression was that they're quite tasty 😋

The kelp topping is shredded and makes a nice accent. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a firm texture, and I was bothered that a bit of sinewy texture remained. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), by contrast, were stewed until meltingly tender, but these also seemed to have a slight sinewy texture left.
As it turns out, this shop also has a sister shop in Osaka. It's great that you can enjoy the taste of Okinawa on the mainland too 😄

Rating (9/15): When you come to Kin Town, why not stop by between watching the baseball camp? Especially for baseball fans, I think it'll be a rare spot where you can enjoy a meal while gazing at the players' autographs 😊

南乃畑.name: Minami no Hata
南乃畑.desc: An Okinawan restaurant with an attached farmers' market inside "Wansaka Oura Park" on Nago's east coast. It's particular about fresh local ingredients such as meat and vegetables, and its signature is the "Minami no Hata Soba," topped with everything—pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and pork spare ribs (soki)—plus fuchiba (mugwort). There are outdoor tables too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map," and I ate here in February 2021 😄
Minami no Hata (inside Wansaka Oura Park)
In the "Nago Soba Map," "Minami no Hata" is featured as shop 21 of 41
Minami no Hata is apparently particular about fresh ingredients, using local meat and vegetables. This time I ordered the "Minami no Hata Soba," which was introduced in the soba map 😄
Minami no Hata Soba　¥800
A soup with bonito flavor and rich broth, topped with everything—jiggly pig's feet (tebichi), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), and pork spare ribs (soki)—plus fuchiba (mugwort). Solidly tasty 😁

Rating (9/15): It's also fairly close to "Kanucha Bay Resort" from here, so how about it when you're staying there, or driving or sightseeing along the east coast of northern Okinawa Island? It's a quiet place, so on a nice day, how about a leisurely meal at the outdoor tables? ✌

南部そば.name: Nanbu Soba
南部そば.desc: Provisional #7 (13.5/15). A popular shop on the Itoman Road where the parking lot is full even before opening. Its selling point is the "Nanbu Soba," with two large, jiggly pig's feet (tebichi) stewed in black vinegar and ginger. Bonito-based soup with homemade medium-thin wavy noodles. Rated No.1 in the southern area.
t: In November 2022, on my way back from surfing at Suicide Cliff Point in Itoman, I tried eating here lol　It's along the National Route 331 bypass (Itoman Road), so it's easy to find.
It had only just opened (from 11:00), but the parking lot was already full lol
It had only just opened (from 11:00), but the parking lot in front of the shop was already full

I arrived right around the opening time of 11:00, but the parking lot in front of the shop already looked full. I thought it might be tough to eat here, but they also have a second? third? parking lot a little way off behind the shop, and after lining up for a bit, I made it inside safely ☺
When I went inside and looked at the menu, the "Nanbu Soba," which has the same name as the shop, caught my eye, so I ordered it.

Maybe pig's feet (tebichi) (stewed pig's trotters) are this shop's selling point as a topping, because two large pieces of pig's feet (tebichi) were sitting on top of the soba 😁　It was explained that the pig's feet (tebichi) are slowly stewed in a secret sauce with black vinegar and ginger until they're jiggly and soft, and packed with flavor and natural collagen. Looks delicious 🤤
Menu (Nanbu Soba = with two pig's feet/tebichi. Also bone-in pork rib soba (hon-soki), yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) soba, and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba)

This time I ordered the "Nanbu Soba (with two pieces of pig's feet/tebichi)," which shares the shop's name and seems to be its selling point. Some people from the mainland may not like pig's feet (tebichi), but there's also "bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) (Okinawan-style spare ribs, the area around the pork rib bones)" and "yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) (oboro tofu) soba," so I think those would be delicious too.

By the way, in Okinawa a (beef) steak to finish off a night of drinking is also famous, but basically I think pork is the main meat used in Okinawan cuisine. People eat every part of the pig, so much so that it's said "they eat everything except the oink," so pig's feet are delicious too ✌
I ordered the Nanbu Soba (large)　¥970

First, a sip of the soup. The bonito-based soup has a strong flavor, and the noodles are the homemade noodles also advertised on the outside of the building—medium-thin and wavy. They're smooth and chewy, and with the way the soup clings to the noodles, I felt it was delicious and in a higher class than the other shops I've eaten at ☺
This time I felt that, to some extent, "a shop popular enough to have a line = basically delicious" really does hold true. (*There are exceptions, so please be careful)

Rating (13.5/15): At this point (March 2023), I think it's the most delicious Okinawa soba shop in the southern area of Okinawa Island. It's relatively close to Naha Airport too, so how about it for tourists' last meal lol
